{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-scgm","title":"[review] project-LICHEN-worker6-69p2: check_rule validation removed from deserializers","description":"## Bug: Input validation `check_rule()` removed from deserializers

**Location:** 
- `rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs:167` (`Fragment::from_bytes`)
- `rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs:260` (`Ack::from_bytes_for`)

Both `Fragment::from_bytes` and `Ack::from_bytes_for` previously called `check_rule(data[0])?` to validate that the rule_id in the input matches known rule IDs (120 or 121). This validation was removed in this commit.

**Impact:** Unknown/malformed rule IDs are silently accepted rather than rejected with `FragmentError::UnsupportedRule`. This means:
- Corrupted fragments with wrong rule IDs will be accepted and potentially mismatched to the wrong session
- The `rule_id` field in `FragmentReceiver` (which uses sentinel value 0) could accept garbage data that happens to pass other checks

**Note:** `check_rule()` IS still called in both `write_to` methods (`Fragment::write_to` at line 134, `Ack::write_to` at line 220), so the asymmetry is inconsistent.

**Fix:** Restore `check_rule(data[0])?` in both deserialization functions.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"agent@lichen-project.dev","created_at":"2026-07-24T18:53:56.479413611Z","created_by":"AI Agent","updated_at":"2026-07-24T18:53:56.479413611Z"}
